LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 HANDWRITING: NEATNESS AND LEGIBILITY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility, part of Strand 1 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we write instructions? 2. Why should we write neatly and legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. outline letters of the alphabet neatly for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose a paragraph neatly and legibly for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the importance of writing legibly and neatly.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. outline letters of the alphabet neatly for effective communication,

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose a paragraph neatly and legibly for effective communication,

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the importance of writing legibly and neatly.

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. write letters of the alphabet in upper case and lower case neatly,

2. identify various cultural attire from pictures,

3. create target words on flashcards using the letters of the alphabet neatly,

4. work jointly with peers to write a short paragraph neatly and legibly on the theme,

5. share the short paragraphs developed in class for peer review,

6. work collaboratively to organise their neatly written paragraphs in the class portfolio. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. write letters of the alphabet in upper case and lower case neatly,
2. identify various cultural attire from pictures,
3. create target words on flashcards using the letters of the alphabet neatly,
4. work jointly with peers to write a short paragraph neatly and legibly on the theme,
5. share the short paragraphs developed in class for peer review,
6. work collaboratively to organise their neatly written paragraphs in the class portfolio. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner works jointly with peers to create flashcards with words

using letters of the alphabet.

• Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner exchanges new ideas when writing a short paragraph on the

theme neatly and legibly.

6

Values:
• Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to write short paragraphs on the theme neatly and legibly.

• Responsibility: This is achieved as the learner diligently organises their neatly written paragraphs in the class portfolio.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness: This is promoted as the learner interacts with various sources to identify varied cultural attire associated

with the community.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of diverse community cultural attire to citizenship in Social Studies.

7

Suggested Vocabulary: environment, nature, forests, sea, rivers, vegetation, protect, climate, climate change, weather, buildings

Main points to remember:

1. outline letters of the alphabet neatly for effective communication,
2. compose a paragraph neatly and legibly for effective communication,
3. appreciate the importance of writing legibly and neatly.

Remember the key question: How do we write instructions? 2. Why should we write neatly and legibly?
